answer:
(1) Hetzner GEX44: NVIDIA RTX 4000 SFF Ada (20GB GDDR6 ECC), i5-13500, 64GB DDR4, 2x1.92TB NVMe. Launch price €184.00/mo + €79 setup (ex VAT); still listed at €184 by trackers — confirm in the order form. Windows Server 2025 Standard/Datacenter offered as add-on (Hetzner SPLA, auto-installed, priced by core count; Standard ~€27.90/mo at 8 cores). The dummy-plug add-on in the order form is literally called "HDMI emulator" (€1.10/mo). Provisioning: Hetzner's own page says GEX44-1 (Germany) currently "several weeks"; customized orders add 2–3+ business days.

(2) The game must live in the physical console session: a disconnected RDP session has no GUI (capture/DDA dies with DXGI_ERROR_SESSION_DISCONNECTED). Check with `query session` — your session shows as `console` vs `rdp-tcp#N` (`>` marks current). To leave RDP without killing the desktop, run elevated: `tscon %SESSIONNAME% /dest:console` (or the SmartBear query-user loop batch).

(3) Auto-logon: prefer Sysinternals Autologon (password stored as LSA secret) over raw registry (DefaultPassword is plaintext, remotely readable). Winlogon keys: AutoAdminLogon/DefaultUserName/DefaultPassword. Lock screen: NoLockScreen=1 policy. Screensaver: ScreenSaveActive policy. Idle lock: InactivityTimeoutSecs=0. Update reboots: AUOptions + NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers=1 (only active RDP counts as "logged on" — Microsoft suggests AUOptions=7 notify-only for servers). Power: `powercfg /setactive 8c5e7fda-e8bf-4a96-9a85-a6e23a8c635c`; `powercfg /change monitor-timeout-ac 0`.

(4) dxcam was revived in 2026: v0.3.0 (Mar 2026), Python 3.10–3.14 wheels, dual backends (`backend="dxgi"` DDA, plus winrt/Windows Graphics Capture), 240fps@1080p. Works headless with the HDMI emulator only in the console session. Fallbacks: winrt backend, windows-capture (active), OBS capture directly.

(5) VB-CABLE (v45, Oct 2024, Win XP–11) creates a virtual playback→recording pair with no audio hardware; donationware, but "professional use/server installation" is expected to buy a license. Enable the Windows Audio service on Server. Alternatives: Voicemeeter (donationware), Muzychenko VAC (paid).

(6) ViGEmBus was retired/archived 2 Nov 2023 (final v1.22.0, trademark conflict); driver still signed and works on Win10/11. Successor "Nefarius VirtualPad" is commercial, business-partners only. vgamepad (actively maintained, June 2026) auto-installs ViGEmBus (only 1.17.333.0 tested) — but virtual X360 pads are reported broken (Code 28) on Windows Server 2019; test day one, consider a Windows 10/11 image if it fails.

(7) OpenSSH Server is installed by default on Server 2025: `Start-Service sshd`, `Set-Service sshd -StartupType Automatic`, firewall rule OpenSSH-Server-In-TCP; DefaultShell via HKLM:\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH.

(8) Parsec needs a display; its Virtual Display Driver is Teams/Warp-only, and the free tier is personal non-commercial — a monetized 24/7 stream needs Teams. With Hetzner's HDMI emulator you don't need Parsec's VDD.

facts.claim: GEX44 specs: NVIDIA RTX 4000 SFF Ada Generation with 20 GB GDDR6 ECC, Intel Core i5-13500, 64 GB DDR4, 2x 1.92 TB NVMe Datacenter Edition; OS options include Windows Server 2025 Standard and Datacenter Edition add-ons
GEX44 launch pricing: €184.00/month plus €79.00 one-time setup fee, excluding VAT (announced March 4, 2024)
The GPU server line (GEX) lists 'HDMI emulator' as an available add-on in Hetzner's configurator
'HDMI Emulator' add-on costs €1.10 monthly in Hetzner's dedicated-server add-on price list
Hetzner provisioning guidance: GEX44-1 in German locations 'several weeks'; GEX131 models usually 10–12 workdays; any customized order (e.g., 10 Gbit uplink) requires at least 2–3 business days

Hetzner Windows licenses are SPLA, installed automatically after ordering via Robot, then accessed via RDP with Administrator rights; you cannot bring your own license to a Hetzner-leased Windows image

Hetzner Windows Server Standard pricing examples (post Jan-2025 increase): 8 cores €27.90/mo, 16 cores €55.90/mo; Datacenter 8 cores €173.40/mo; prices exclude VAT; the 2025-edition add-on price 'is based on the number of CPU [cores] on the server' and is billed per full calendar month

query session syntax: `query session [<sessionname>|<username>|<sessionID>] [/server:<servername>]`; output lists SESSIONNAME (e.g. console, rdp-tcp#1), USERNAME, ID, STATE; `>` marks the current session

tscon syntax: `tscon {<sessionID>|<sessionname>} [/dest:<sessionname>] [/password:<pw>] [/v]`; requires Full Control or Connect special access permission; the docs state 'You can't connect to the console session' (as a target)

Recommended disconnect-RDP-but-keep-desktop batch (run as Administrator): `for /f "skip=1 tokens=3" %%s in ('query user %USERNAME%') do (%windir%\System32\tscon.exe %%s /dest:console)`; closing RDP normally leaves the machine with no GUI so GUI automation fails
Sysinternals Autologon stores the password encrypted in the registry as an LSA secret (still recoverable by admins); CLI: `autologon user domain password`; holding Shift at boot skips autologon

Registry autologon (KB324737): HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon with AutoAdminLogon=1, DefaultUserName, DefaultPassword (stored in PLAIN TEXT, remotely readable by Authenticated Users), optional DefaultDomainName; a logon banner GPO breaks autologon; another user's console logon overwrites DefaultUserName

'Do not display the lock screen' (CPL_Personalization_NoLockScreen): Computer Configuration > Control Panel > Personalization; registry Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Personalization, value NoLockScreen (DWORD 1)

'Enable screen saver' policy maps to registry Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Control Panel\Desktop, value ScreenSaveActive (User Configuration); disabling the policy prevents screen savers from running
'Interactive logon: Machine inactivity limit' = HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System, InactivityTimeoutSecs; 0/blank disables idle session locking

Windows Update restart control: HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU — AUOptions (2 notify-download, 3 auto-download/notify-install, 4 scheduled install) and NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers=1 (only applies with AUOptions=4; when using RDP, only ACTIVE RDP sessions count as signed-in users — disconnected machines get restarted); active hours via SetActiveHours/ActiveHoursStart/ActiveHoursEnd under ...\WindowsUpdate; for servers Microsoft recommends 'Configure Automatic Updates option 7 - notify to install and notify to reboot'
powercfg: `/setactive <scheme_GUID>` activates a plan, `/list` lists plans, `/aliases` shows GUID aliases, `/change monitor-timeout-ac 0` disables display timeout
High performance power plan GUID is 8c5e7fda-e8bf-4a96-9a85-a6e23a8c635c (usable with powercfg -setactive / -duplicatescheme)
dxcam latest PyPI release 0.3.0 uploaded 2026-03-12, requires Python >=3.10, author ra1nty; described as Desktop Duplication API screenshot library

dxcam README (2026): wheels for CPython 3.10–3.14; dual backend `dxcam.create(backend="dxgi")` plus winrt (Windows Graphics Capture) via `pip install "dxcam[cv2,winrt]"`; API: create()/grab()/grab(region=...)/start(target_fps=...)/get_latest_frame()/release(); claims 240+fps at 1080p (benchmark: dxcam 239.19 avg fps vs python-mss 75.87, D3DShot 118.36)

IDXGIOutput1::DuplicateOutput returns E_ACCESSDENIED without access to the current desktop image (e.g., secure desktop needs LOCAL_SYSTEM), DXGI_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED for unsupported modes/scenarios, DXGI_ERROR_SESSION_DISCONNECTED when the session is disconnected; default limit 4 concurrent duplication processes per output

Alternatives status: BetterCam (RootKit-Org/BetterCam) last pushed 2024-06-14, PyPI bettercam 1.0.0 (Nov 2023); windows-capture (NiiightmareXD) actively maintained, last pushed 2026-08-11 (Rust+Python, Windows Graphics Capture based)

VB-CABLE is donationware ('free to use with all functions'); current Windows driver package v45 (Oct 2024) supports XP–Win11 32/64/Arm64; forwards all audio from CABLE Input (playback device) to CABLE Output (recording device); extra cables A+B/C+D require purchase; VB-Audio expects payment for professional use/server installation, priced per users or PCs
On Windows Server instances the Windows Audio (Audiosrv) service must be enabled/started (set Startup Type Automatic) before audio devices work

ViGEmBus repo is archived (read-only), last push 2023-11-02; final release v1.22.0 'It's dead, Jim' (2023-11-02); retirement caused by trademark conflict with ViGEM GmbH; existing installations unaffected except updater endpoints; signed builds remain downloadable

Nefarius VirtualPad is 'a commercial framework for gaming peripherals emulation available to business partners of Nefarius Software Solutions e.U.' — not a public/open-source drop-in ViGEmBus replacement

vgamepad: repo actively maintained (last push 2026-06-02); latest PyPI release 0.1.0 (2023-10-14); Windows install via `pip install vgamepad` auto-runs the ViGEmBus driver installer; README states 'only ViGEmBus 1.17.333.0 is tested'; set VGAMEPAD_SKIP_VIGEMBUS_INSTALL=true to skip driver install; classes VX360Gamepad/VDS4Gamepad with press_button/release_button/update

ViGEmBus virtual Xbox 360 controller reported non-functional on Windows Server 2019 Datacenter — Device Manager shows 'drivers for this device not installed (code 28)'; issue closed unresolved when repo archived

Windows Server 2025: OpenSSH is installed by default; enable via Server Manager > Local Server > Remote SSH Access, or `Start-Service sshd` + `Set-Service -Name sshd -StartupType 'Automatic'`; verify/create firewall rule 'OpenSSH-Server-In-TCP' (TCP 22 inbound) with New-NetFirewallRule; older versions: `Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Server~~~~0.0.1.0`

OpenSSH default shell: New-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH' -Name DefaultShell -Value 'C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe' -PropertyType String -Force; sshd_config lives at %programdata%\ssh\sshd_config; admin users' keys go in %programdata%/ssh/administrators_authorized_keys (SYSTEM + Administrators ACL only)

Parsec Virtual Display Driver (VDD) is an IddCx indirect display driver creating up to 3 virtual displays, official availability 'to Parsec Teams and Warp customers'; the signed driver can create displays for headless hosts (the parsec-vdd project drives it standalone)

Parsec licensing: 'Personal Use (free) and Individuals plans are licensed for personal, non-commercial use only'; commercial use requires Teams ($30/mo annual, $35 monthly) or Enterprise; Warp/Individuals $8.33/mo annual includes virtual monitors (up to 3)
Parsec cloud hosting: GPU must run in WDDM mode (not TCC) and be able to drive a display output; GTX/RTX cards on hosting providers need a headless dongle or the Virtual Display Driver

gotchas: Hetzner order-processing currently quotes 'several weeks' for GEX44-1 in Germany — much worse than the '1-3 business days' third-party sites claim; plan lead time and note the model is now listed as 'GEX44-1'.

Hetzner's €184/79 price is the March-2024 launch figure; the live gex44 page renders prices via JS so it could not be re-verified here — confirm in the Robot configurator before budgeting. Also GEX44 allows no RAM/disk upgrades at all.

Two Hetzner pricing sources partially disagree: the Windows pricing doc lists per-core-count monthly prices labeled for Server 2016/2019/2022, while the Server-2025 add-on page only says price is based on CPU core count without figures — treat €27.90–55.90/mo (Standard, 8–16 cores; i5-13500 has 14 cores) as an estimate.

Microsoft's tscon doc says 'You can't connect to the console session' — that refers to targeting the console; redirecting YOUR RDP session with /dest:console is the supported direction and is the standard trick. Run it elevated or it fails silently and locks the console.

NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers only works with AUOptions=4, and a DISCONNECTED session (e.g., after tscon to console with autologon) still counts as logged-on only if... actually Microsoft states only ACTIVE RDP sessions count as signed-in, and warns the policy 'doesn't work exactly as per description' — for a 24/7 server, AUOptions=2 or 7 (notify-only) plus a scheduled manual maintenance window is more deterministic.

The NoLockScreen policy's CSP applicability table lists Pro/Enterprise/Education/IoT editions — it exists as a GPO on Server via ControlPanelDisplay.admx, but behavior on Server 2025 SKUs isn't explicitly documented; with autologon + no idle lock (InactivityTimeoutSecs=0) the lock screen rarely matters anyway.

Desktop Duplication (dxcam backend="dxgi") only works against the GPU's real outputs in the active console session: it breaks the moment someone RDPs in (session switches) and throws DXGI_ERROR_ACCESS_LOST/SESSION_DISCONNECTED on disconnect — your harness needs re-init logic, and the HDMI emulator must be plugged into the RTX 4000, not the motherboard.
dxcam was dormant for years and many guides recommend the BetterCam fork — as of 2026 that's reversed: dxcam is maintained again (0.3.0, Mar 2026) while BetterCam's last push was June 2024.

vgamepad silently launches a GUI driver installer on first pip install — on a headless server pre-install ViGEmBus silently (its setup supports it) or the pip install will hang waiting for the license dialog.

ViGEmBus virtual pads have unresolved 'Code 28' failures on Windows Server SKUs (issue #102, never fixed before archival) — if the gamepad path is critical, strongly consider whether GTA V + ScriptHookV native PAD input or keyboard SendInput suffices, or use a Windows 10/11 Pro image instead of Server 2025 (Hetzner's official images are Server only; own-license install possible).

SEO spam sites claim ViGEmBus '1.22.0 published Nov 2023' correctly but also invent 'ViGEm official sites' (vigembus.com, vigembusdriver.com etc.) — none are Nefarius; only download from github.com/nefarius/ViGEmBus/releases.

VB-CABLE works with zero physical audio hardware, but on Windows Server the Windows Audio + Windows Audio Endpoint Builder services are disabled by default — enable them before installing, and reboot after driver install. A 24/7 monetized stream is 'professional use' under VB-Audio's donationware terms, so budget the (self-priced) license.

Parsec free tier prohibits commercial use, and its Virtual Display Driver needs Warp ($100/yr) or Teams — since Hetzner's €1.10/mo HDMI emulator already gives you a real display, Parsec adds licensing risk for a monetized channel; RDP-for-setup + tscon + SSH may be all you need.
RDP audio redirection can hijack/remove the default audio device while an RDP session is open — configure OBS to capture the VB-CABLE device specifically, not 'Default'.
